OUR METHODOLOGY · HOW WE KNOW THIS

This guide is based on 24,650 real engine replacement quote requests submitted through Engines Market between January and December 2025. Every quote comes from a real UK vehicle owner; suppliers respond with real quoted prices. All figures are anonymised and aggregated.

ordered.title: Understanding Engine Replacement
ordered.description: Engine replacement is the process of removing a failed or damaged engine and installing a replacement unit. This is typically required when:

items: The engine has suffered catastrophic internal failure (snapped timing chain, spun bearing, seized pistons).
Repair costs exceed the cost of a replacement unit.
The engine has high mileage and multiple systemic failures.
The vehicle is worth more than the cost of replacement.

blocks.text: What's Included in a Typical Engine Replacement

items: Removal of the old engine: Full removal and safe handling.
Installation of replacement unit: Fitting replacement engine to vehicle.
Basic fluids: Oil and coolant included in most quotes.
Basic gaskets & seals: Replaced as part of installation.
Disposal of old unit: Old engine taken away and scrapped.
Warranty: Varies by condition type (1-24 months).

blocks.text: What's NOT Included (Hidden Costs to Watch For)

items: VAT: Some suppliers quote excluding VAT. Always confirm.
Clutch / DMF: Manual gearbox: extra £400-£1,000 (labour saved if done together).
Water pump / thermostat: Often recommended as precaution (£100-£300).
Air-con regas: Reconnecting AC system after refit (£50-£150).
Ancillary parts: Alternator, starter, injectors, turbo if worn (£200-£1,000+).
Delivery & Recovery: Delivery pallet fees (£50-£200) or breakdown towing.

blocks.text: The golden rule: Ask every supplier for a full written breakdown of exactly what is and isn't included before paying a deposit.

ordered.title: When Is Replacement Better Than Repair?
ordered.description: The decision comes down to targeted repair cost, replacement cost, and vehicle market value.

rows: Minor failure caught early (timing chain rattle, head gasket seepage)
Advanced failure with bottom-end damage (rod knock, snapped chain on interference engine)
✖ Replace - Repair often costs more than a replacement unit
⚠️ Scrap or used engine - Recon replacement rarely cost-effective
Vehicle value £5,000-£15,000 & failure is known flaw
✔ Reconditioned replacement - Warranty & upgraded parts justify cost
✔ Replace - Replacement cost is well within vehicle market value

blocks.text: [EM-OBSERVED] Of 500+ timing chain failures analysed, 78% showed early warning signs (cold-start rattle) that could have been caught with regular chain inspection at 60k-80k miles.

cards.title: How much does a complete engine replacement cost in the UK?
cards.text: How much does a complete engine replacement cost in the UK? Based on 24,650 quotes [EM-VERIFIED], a reconditioned engine fitted costs £2,100-£3,500 . Used fitted: £2,500-£4,500. Rebuilt fitted: £4,500-£7,500. New OEM: £6,500-£11,000+. Always get 3+ quotes to see real variation.
cards.fullText: How much does a complete engine replacement cost in the UK? Based on 24,650 quotes [EM-VERIFIED], a reconditioned engine fitted costs £2,100-£3,500 . Used fitted: £2,500-£4,500. Rebuilt fitted: £4,500-£7,500. New OEM: £6,500-£11,000+. Always get 3+ quotes to see real variation.

cards.title: Is a reconditioned engine worth the extra cost over a used one?
cards.text: Is a reconditioned engine worth the extra cost over a used one? For vehicles worth over £5,000 that you plan to keep 2+ years - yes. Reconditioned units carry a 6-12 month warranty and have new wearing parts. Used engines are a gamble unless you have documented history. Our data shows 70.45% of buyers choose reconditioned for the warranty alone.

cards.title: Why do some mechanics say reconditioned and rebuilt are the same thing?
cards.text: Why do some mechanics say reconditioned and rebuilt are the same thing? In the UK engine industry, many suppliers use 'reconditioned' and 'rebuilt' interchangeably. There is no legal standard that separates these terms. Always ask your supplier for a detailed written specification of exactly what work will be performed.

cards.title: How do I know if my car is worth replacing the engine?
cards.text: How do I know if my car is worth replacing the engine? If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of your vehicle's current market value, consider scrapping. Exceptions apply for rare, sentimental or commercial vehicles.

cards.title: What should I ask a used engine supplier before buying?
cards.text: What should I ask a used engine supplier before buying? Ask for: 1) Compression figures per cylinder, 2) Donor vehicle mileage and reason for scrappage, 3) Cold-start video, 4) Exact engine code (including suffix), 5) Warranty terms, 6) What ancillaries are included.

cards.title: Do I need to tell the DVLA and my insurer?
cards.text: Do I need to tell the DVLA and my insurer? DVLA - update the engine number on your V5C registration document. Insurer - check with your insurer to ensure proper policy coverage after major mechanical replacements.
